title: Adaptive Quantile Thresholding for Continuous Batching and KV Memory Stabilization
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS (production spikes > 6k rps per shard), the continuous batching admission heuristic occasionally oversubscribes microbatch slots, causing KV-cache churn and transient GPU memory pressure that triggers OOMs and elevated latency tails. Existing fixed-threshold rules and simple exponential backoff either underutilize capacity (hurting throughput) or oscillate during bursty traffic.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive quantile-based admission controller that adjusts micro-batching thresholds based on recent tail latency (p95/p99), KV hit-rate, and GPU free memory quantiles. The controller computes sliding-window quantiles instead of raw averages to be robust to bursts, applies hysteresis to avoid oscillation, and exposes a tunable headroom budget per-GPU. Admission decisions combine: (1) estimated per-request token-cost, (2) current kv_hotness_score, and (3) quantile headroom margin to accept/defer.

Goals: (a) reduce tail latency p99 by >= 25% during spikes, (b) reduce KV eviction rate by >= 40%, (c) keep GPU memory OOM incidents at 0 for test clusters, (d) keep throughput loss < 8% under steady load.

Design notes: We use a two-tier controller: local node-level fast-path using in-memory sliding quantile sketches (CKMS or t-digest) with 5s windows for p95/p99; and global coordinator that recommends threshold shifts every 30s based on aggregated telemetry. Hysteresis band and minimum hold time prevents flip-flopping. Admission is additive to existing priority-aware queueing so we can enforce tenant fairness.

Trade-offs: quantile sketches add CPU and memory on CPU control-plane; but they are lightweight compared to GPU cost. Coordination adds 30s lag for large shifts but keeps local fast-path responsive. Conservative default parameters will be applied to avoid regressions.

Instrumentation & rollout: expose metrics: admission_accept_rate, admission_defer_rate, kv_eviction_rate, gpu_free_memory_quantile (p10/p50/p90), local_p99_latency. Create dashboard in Grafana and alerting for deviation. Start with canary on one AZ (dedicated small test cluster), then 10% traffic for 48h, then full rollout if metrics stable.

Acceptance criteria: no increase in 95th latency violation alerts during canary; kv_eviction_rate drop in canary >= 20%; no OOMs.
